prompt: Create one production transparent PNG parallax layer for our rural twilight forest pixel-art game. Image 1 is our previous low-tree layer: retain its overall vertical placement (empty upper ~45% and vegetation confined to lower ~55%) but REDESIGN the foliage. Image 2 is a visual hierarchy reference only: observe how secondary trees use broad readable leaf clusters and restrained contrast; do not copy its composition, buildings, characters, tree species or blue daytime palette. Output wide 1536x1024 RGBA. Six to eight short woodland trees with varied rounded, slightly asymmetric crowns and slim partly concealed trunks, interspersed with understated low shrubs. Uneven spacing with transparent breathing gaps between groups. Use muted warm gray-olive, moss, taupe and dusty ochre, gentle peach-tan highlights, plum-brown shadows; warm rural sunset, but NOT orange/yellow glitter. Make colors visibly softer and less saturated than image1, with a narrow middle-value range and no near-black outlines. Leaves arranged in clear medium-sized pixel clusters (roughly 5-12px at this resolution), rich enough for a finished game but NOT dense single-pixel noise or photographic bark. Distinct silhouette steps, crisp pixel art, no blur. Keep highlights on broad upper planes rather than tracing every leaf. Main silhouettes start around y480..650, trunks descend behind shrubs through bottom edge; taller crowns no higher than y440. Empty upper portion must be fully alpha transparent. Left/right edges end in low shrubs at similar heights for mirrored horizontal repetition. Absolutely NO sky, mist gradients, colored backdrop, floor, soil, platform, roots, giant trunk, text, UI or characters. Deliver only the short trees and shrubs on true transparency. This is a complete replacement for image1, not a composited game screenshot.
